# motor_encoder_switch

<!-- Generated by orb-weaver-kicad-board-docs from board.yaml and board-manifest.yaml; do not edit. -->

Subsystem sheet `/motor_encoder_switch` of **mouse-joystick-pcb**, from the library recipe `orb_weaver:motor_encoder_switch` (`design_subsystems/motor_encoder_switch/motor_encoder_switch.subsystem.yaml`).

Motor, encoder and limit-switch subsystem: a TMC5130 stepper driver with its SPI bus, diagnostics and driver enable tapped for the instrument port, a 5 V quadrature encoder input, a debounced limit-switch input and a DAC80501 analog angle output, with the motor and encoder terminal blocks, the BNC for the analog output and the 10 k pulls on the SPI lines, the diagnostics and the driver enable. The first library recipe (PLANS 2026-09-30 step 4d, D27), derived from the mouse board.

Board note: board-authored sheet, 10 parts

## Notes

- The SPI pulls (SCK, COPI, CIPO to GND; ~{TMC_CS}, ~{DRV_EN}, DIAG0, DIAG1 to +3.3V) are the subsystem's, not the driver block's. They bias nets the board drives, so a second driver on the same bus would not double them (layout conventions, convention 10).
- The instrument taps of the driver's own signals (~{CS}_INST, ~{DRV_EN}_INST, the DIAG taps) come from inside the driver block (convention 14). The shared SPI lines' taps (SCK, COPI and CIPO _INST) sit inside the retired block the mouse board carries and move out when the block is next revised (PLANS, owed to boards).
